summary: Thin day for evidence: Reddit, X, Bluesky and most other platforms were unreachable from the research environment, so every idea here is backed only by Hacker News threads and comments from the last week. The strongest themes were being stonewalled by companies that hold your money or access, disposable phone numbers for OTP-gated signups, and scraped-and-spammed public job threads.

ideas.title: Get-a-Human Escalation Kit
ideas.oneLiner: A per-company escalation ladder, evidence timeline and ready-to-send complaint letters for when support ghosts you or freezes your money.
ideas.problem: People with a frozen balance, a closed account or an expired-warranty download are bounced between departments, ghosted in chat and email, and told 'nothing further is needed' while nothing happens. They don't know the next rung: regulator, ombudsman, executive contact, or the formal complaint wording that forces a response.
ideas.targetUsers: Freelancers and small-business owners whose payment provider or bank closes an account, plus consumers stuck with warranty, refund or account-lockout disputes. In India, anyone who needs the RBI Ombudsman, National Consumer Helpline or CPGRAMS route.
ideas.monetization: Free template library; one-time ₹199–₹499 per case for the guided case file (timeline, evidence PDF, auto-drafted regulator complaint); optional small-business plan around ₹799/month.
mvp: Pick a company type (payment provider, bank, telecom, e-commerce, hardware warranty) and get its escalation ladder with regulator and ombudsman links for India/US/EU
Case timeline logger: paste emails and chat transcripts, get a dated evidence summary
Complaint letter generator citing the timeline, ticket numbers and the contradicting replies
Follow-up reminders that escalate to the next rung after N days of silence
Export a single PDF case file to send to the regulator or a chargeback team

competitors.name: GetHuman
competitors.gap: Not verified today. Known as a directory of phone shortcuts to reach company support; it does not appear to manage a multi-step escalation with evidence and regulator letters.

competitors.name: DoNotPay
competitors.gap: Not verified today. Positioned as a general consumer-rights bot rather than a case file focused on frozen funds and account closures.

ideas.title: Disposable Phone Number for OTP Signups
ideas.oneLiner: A 'temp mail' for phone numbers: a real, non-VoIP-flagged number you can burn after receiving a verification code.
ideas.problem: Sites demand a phone number for SMS verification, and people don't want to hand over their real one. Free web 'receive SMS' sites get blocked, and Google Voice numbers are rejected by some sites, so users have no reliable throwaway option.
ideas.targetUsers: Privacy-conscious users tired of spam calls and data-broker leaks, people signing up for many services, and developers or QA testers who need verification numbers.
ideas.monetization: Pay-per-number credits (about ₹20–₹60 per 24h number) or a monthly bundle; free tier limited to a few lower-reliability numbers.
mvp: Rent a number for 20 minutes to 7 days, with the SMS inbox shown in the app
Push notification and copy-to-clipboard for the OTP
Country selection with a per-site success-rate indicator
Auto-burn after the code arrives, with a refund if no SMS comes
Android SMS provider integration (Twilio or a local aggregator) behind a thin backend

ideas.title: Contact Shield for Public Hiring Threads
ideas.oneLiner: Post a throwaway relay address in 'Who wants to be hired' threads; only senders who pass a verified-opportunity check reach your real inbox.
ideas.problem: Job seekers who post their email in public hiring threads are scraped within days and flooded with job-board pitches, fake recruiters and malware 'coding challenges'. Some then stop posting, even though real offers do come from those threads.
ideas.targetUsers: Freelancers and job seekers posting on Hacker News, Reddit and similar boards, including Indian developers looking for remote roles.
ideas.monetization: Free for one alias; ₹149/month for multiple aliases, sender screening rules and auto-replies. Possible light sponsorship from verified recruiters.
mvp: Generate a per-thread alias such as name+hn-oct@domain that forwards to your inbox
Auto-triage: block mails matching job-board pitch patterns and unknown free-mail 'recruiters'
Require a short verified-opportunity form (company, role, pay range) before forwarding
One-click kill switch to burn the alias after the thread ends
Digest email of what was blocked, so real offers aren't lost

competitors.name: SimpleLogin / Firefox Relay / Apple Hide My Email
competitors.gap: Not verified today. These are general email aliases; they forward everything and don't screen for legitimate recruiter offers.

competitors.name: Disposable email addresses
competitors.gap: One commenter says a fresh disposable address stopped the spam, but it also blocked legitimate non-test messages, which leaves no way to receive real offers.

ideas.title: Git-Backed Wiki Non-Developers Can Edit
ideas.oneLiner: A fast team wiki that stores plain markdown in a git repo but gives non-developers a friendly editor.
ideas.problem: Developers call Confluence bloated and slow with a bad editor, but the common alternative, git plus markdown, locks non-developers out of editing. Teams are stuck choosing between a tool engineers dislike and one the rest of the company can't use.
ideas.targetUsers: Small engineering teams and agencies that also have PMs, support and ops staff who need to edit internal docs.
ideas.monetization: Per-seat SaaS, around ₹250 per editor per month with free read-only viewers; self-host licence for teams that want to keep data in their own repo.
mvp: Connect a GitHub repo and render its markdown folder as a wiki
WYSIWYG editor that commits to a branch and opens a PR or auto-merges for trusted editors
Instant full-text search
Page tree, backlinks and simple permissions per folder
Import from Confluence export

ideas.title: App Store Review Queue Tracker
ideas.oneLiner: Crowdsourced live iOS App Review wait times, with alerts when your build is slower than the current median.
ideas.problem: Indie developers report iOS review times stretching from under a day to a week or more, and have no way to know whether their wait is normal or a sign of a problem. Commenters attribute the slowdown to a flood of low-quality apps.
ideas.targetUsers: Indie iOS and Flutter developers submitting apps and updates to the App Store.
ideas.monetization: Free public dashboard; ₹299/month for private-team alerts, webhook to Slack/Telegram, and per-category history.
mvp: Submit-your-wait form (submission date, review start, outcome, app category)
Live median and p90 review time, with a 30-day trend
Alert when your own submission passes the current p90
Telegram/email notification when status changes
Public API and embeddable widget

competitors.name: Existing App Review time trackers
competitors.gap: Not verified today; whether any current tracker offers per-submission alerts and category-level breakdowns is unconfirmed.
